item.title: Tropical Storm Edouard makes landfall in Louisiana, brings heavy rain to Texas
item.description: Tropical Storm Edouard made landfall in Louisiana Tuesday afternoon, and is also forecast to bring heavy rain to Texas, the National Hurricane Center said.

item.title: Lindsay Clancy trial jury deadlocked, leaves for day without verdict
item.description: The jury in Lindsay Clancy's murder trial told the judge Tuesday morning they are deadlocked, and left a Massachusetts courtroom hours later without reaching a verdict.

item.title: Here's how much interest a $100,000 18-month CD can earn savers now
item.description: A $100,000 18-month CD can produce a big return for savers who act now. This is how much interest they'll earn.

item.title: Trump says new U.S. strikes on Iran in retaliation for sea mines, targeting base
item.description: Two oil tankers were attacked in the Strait of Hormuz as the U.S. and Iran returned to hostilities in a six-month war that appears to be locked in a stalemate.

item.title: How much will a $75,000 home equity loan cost monthly if opened now?
item.description: Need to borrow $75,000 right now? Here's how much it would cost per month if you did so with a home equity loan.

item.title: Rising bond yields threaten to push up U.S. borrowing costs, experts say
item.description: The U.S. bond market influences how much American consumers pay for loans and the interest they can earn on their savings accounts.

item.title: Why a mortgage rate lock makes sense this September
item.description: A mortgage interest rate lock this September, as unconventional as it may seem, may make financial sense. Here's why.

item.title: Modest pay hikes next year could leave some workers lagging inflation
item.description: Employers are likely to offer limited salary increases in 2027 amid ongoing economic uncertainty, according to a survey of 1,000 businesses.

item.title: Texas and Louisiana residents brace for severe storms as Tropical Storm Edouard approaches
item.description: People in Texas and Louisiana are bracing for heavy rain and floods from Tropical Storm Edouardo as it barrels toward the coast. CBS News' Jason Allen has more.

item.title: Supporters coming to Lindsay Clancy trial to meet attorney Kevin Reddington
item.description: A number of people have come to the Massachusetts courthouse where Lindsay Clancy's trial is being held because they want to meet her defense attorney, Kevin Reddington. CBS News' Shanelle Kaul reports.

item.title: Whistleblower warns about USPS' new mail ballot system
item.description: A whistleblower has issued a warning of "potentially catastrophic problems" with the U.S. Postal Service's new system for handling mail ballots. CBS News election law expert and political contributor David Becker has more.

item.title: Ex-Border Patrol commander Bovino was under investigation when he retired
item.description: CBP informed Gregory Bovino in an email on March 2 that the agency was "conducting an official Inquiry into allegations of misconduct reported to CBP." He initiated retirement 16 days later.

item.title: Maps and charts show record number of measles cases in U.S. this year
item.description: CBS News has been tracking a record number of measles cases and outbreaks around the country in 2026. The majority of cases are among those who haven't been vaccinated.

item.title: Congress passes funding bill to avoid shutdown before midterms
item.description: The House on Tuesday passed a measure to extend government funding into December, averting a shutdown in the final stretch of the midterm campaign.

item.title: IRS audit revenue plunged following mass layoffs, watchdog finds
item.description: IRS audits collected $3.5 billion less in fiscal 2025 as the agency shed thousands of auditors and other agency staffers.

item.title: Tony Romo pleads no contest to Wisconsin operating while intoxicated charge
item.description: The longtime Dallas Cowboys quarterback and CBS Sports football analyst said he came to rely on alcohol to get off pain medications after multiple back surgeries.

item.title: U.S. launches new strikes against Iran, CENTCOM says
item.description: The U.S. launched strikes against Iran after tankers in the Strait of Hormuz were hit, CENTCOM said Tuesday afternoon. CBS News' Eleanor Watson and Weijia Jiang have more.

item.title: Judge to decide if Tyler Robinson will stand trial in Charlie Kirk's killing
item.description: A judge in Utah will decide Tuesday whether Tyler Robinson will stand trial for the killing of conservative activist Charlie Kirk. CBS News' Carter Evans has more.

item.title: What the judge told the Lindsay Clancy jury after they said they're deadlocked
item.description: The jury in Lindsay Clancy's murder trial told the judge in the case on Tuesday that they're deadlocked. Deliberations have been ongoing for four days. CBS News' Shanelle Kaul and Rebecca Roiphe have more.

item.title: How much does a $50,000 annuity pay per month in 2026?
item.description: A $50,000 annuity can generate extra retirement income, but the monthly payout varies widely. Here's how — and why.

item.title: Ford recalls nearly 149,000 Mustang vehicles over potential power issue
item.description: A potential wiring issue could lead to vehicles losing power or disruption of other functions, such as windshield wipers and headlights.

item.title: Woman killed in Times Square stabbing identified as Bank of America executive
item.description: A Bank of America executive was fatally stabbed during an attack in New York City's Times Square. CBS News' Jared Ocacher reports.

item.title: Victim in Times Square stabbing identified as Bank of America employee
item.description: Erin Piacenti was identified as one of the two people stabbed by a woman Monday afternoon in Times Square before police shot and killed the suspect.

item.title: Key Massachusetts primary races to follow
item.description: Voters are at the polls Tuesday in Massachusetts to vote in some key primaries ahead of the 2026 midterms. CBS News' Fin Gomez has more.

item.title: DHS chief shares update on New York criminal crackdown operation
item.description: Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin shared an update on Operation Rotten Apple, a crackdown on criminals in New York. CBS News' Nicole Sganga reports.

item.title: U.K. man accused of drugging, abusing wife with other men goes on trial
item.description: The case has drawn parallels to that of Gisèle Pelicot, who publicly testified against her ex-husband in a 2024 mass rape trial.

item.title: Whistleblower warns Postal Service's mail ballot portal is "rushed," "untested"
item.description: The whistleblower, described by lawyers as a federal official, disclosed information about the Postal Service's new mail-voting procedures to Democratic Sen. Richard Blumenthal of Connecticut.

item.title: 3 friends went hiking in the Grand Canyon. 2 died, 1 is still missing.
item.description: At least two people were killed after flash floods swept through parts of Grand Canyon National Park over the weekend.

item.title: 17-year-old girl indicted in San Diego mosque shooting over livestream
item.description: A 17-year-old North Carolina girl has been charged with murder by aiding and abetting in connection with the deadly rampage at the Islamic Center of San Diego in May.

item.title: Melinda French Gates: It Took Three Doctors to Diagnose My Perimenopause
item.description:
Melinda French Gates is focusing her money and attention on improving women's healthcare in America. In Healthful's first episode, French Gates tells Norah O'Donnell why it took three doctors to catch her perimenopause and shares the three simple things that keep her healthier than ever.
